proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique; proposed by NRS_484B_113_3 this iteration

proposals.name: p.left_turn_max_angle
proposals.convention: Upper bound of a left turn, above which the direction of travel counts as reversed (a U-turn).
proposals.source: junction turning geometry; proposed by NRS_484B_227_1_o3 this iteration

proposals.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
proposals.convention: Lower bound of a turn: a leftward heading change below it is a drift or lane change, not a turn onto another way.
proposals.source: junction turning geometry; proposed by NRS_484B_227_1_o3 this iteration

proposals.name: p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance
proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the projected closest approach below which the body of a passenger vehicle and a pedestrian would touch or nearly touch: about a design passenger car's half-length plus a pedestrian's body radius.
proposals.source: design passenger car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P) and pedestrian body ellipse (HCM)

proposals.name: p.rest_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Stop-detection noise floor: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement, set at the resolution of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation from movement is recognized despite sensor jitter.
proposals.source: speed-sensor resolution; proposed by LVMC_11_30_030 this iteration

proposals.name: p.right_turn_max_angle
proposals.convention: Upper bound of a right turn, above which the direction of travel counts as reversed.
proposals.source: junction turning geometry, mirrored from the left-turn band

proposals.name: p.right_turn_min_angle

gaps.proposal: `ru.disabled` | a vehicle that cannot move under its own power (a breakdown, crash damage, a lost wheel or a flat tyre), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a halt, hazard lamps lit or an engine stopped | general
nearest: sig.hazard: 'both indicators flashing together' (a lamp state, not whether the vehicle can move)
kin.engine_running: 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt' (a stopped engine is no disablement, and a disabled vehicle may run its engine)

proposals.name: p.offroad_stop_reach
proposals.convention: Distance within which an off-road standing place counts as practicable for a halting vehicle: the braking distance of a moderate approach, within which the driver can halt on it instead.
proposals.source: stopping-distance model (AASHTO Green Book)

proposals.name: p.queue_gap
proposals.convention: Gap to a halted road user ahead in the lane within which a halt counts as made to avoid conflict with it: a queued vehicle's standstill spacing plus a margin.
proposals.source: queue standstill spacing (HCM)

proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel
proposals.convention: Side-friction limit of horizontal curve design: the lateral acceleration a curve may impose on a vehicle at a comfortable, safe speed.
proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, horizontal curve side friction factors

proposals.name: p.lane_width_speed_time
proposals.convention: Lane width per unit of speed from the lane-width and design-speed relation of highway design guides (a full-width lane for a high design speed): the speed times it may not exceed the lane's width.
proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book lane widths by design speed

proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from the appearance of a hazard to the application of the brakes.
proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance

proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_dry
proposals.convention: Deceleration a driver attains in a controlled stop on a dry paved surface.
proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book and braking studies (Fambro et al., NCHRP 400)

proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_ice
proposals.convention: Deceleration attainable on an icy or snow-covered surface, from the low friction coefficient of such surfaces.
proposals.source: winter road friction measurements (PIARC)

proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_wet
proposals.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers attain on a wet pavement.
proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance
